The best way I know to describe this stuff is called 'mood affiliation'. It's a strange term, but once you get what it means, then the name fits pretty well.

Imagine a typical lefty person on one hand, and a typical righty person on the other. Their affiliation with their respective group is very important to them, it's their tribe, their people. The shared values, shared aspirations, and shared world view represents the world they want to inhabit. It's perfectly fine, and everyone gets to chose for themselves what they like.

Now, mention a topic in front of these groups, say, "black violence" or "abortion". This will evoke a certain mood in each group, a certain response. The details of the response will vary with the fashion of the time, but the mood, the emotion is the important thing. You experience your affiliation with your group by sharing this mood. If your affiliation is important to you, then the mood is important, too.

Mood affiliation.

It's perfectly normal and healthy and we all do it, we just do it in different ways. Most of us refer to our most important affiliations as our values or our principles. Think about what your principles are, and how they tie you to the people you respect, to the world you want to be a part of. Your values and principles are the badges of your tribe.

This is what newspapers sell, and that's why so many people are eager to enjoy it. This is why the facts don't really matter, and why the gut response to the headlines is what it's all about for them.

The only thing that makes some people different - and I include myself in the category, and perhaps it applies to you as well - is that some people belong to a tribe that likes the facts, and likes for things not to be cut and dried. That does not make us better, or even really different. We're just a different flavor of the same thing, just as human and flawed as everyone else, we just value a different style and a different focus. We express our mood affiliation by saying, "hey, wait, there's more to this". That's what our tribe does.

We're just another tribe. The way we feel about ourselves is the same as the way they feel about themselves. We like to think we are smarter and better adapted to the world and less deluded, but they feel that way, too.
